name: Vault Sprout
text: A seed in the vault has split its casing. In the night its roots felt their way along the inner hull, looking for light, and found the seams between the plates. The botanist names it a hull-tree, the kind the first ships were grown from.

results.text: You give it water and a window. By morning the roots have knit a new chamber onto the hull, still green and warm to the touch.
The cuttings will trade well at any orchard. You wrap them in damp cloth and stow them with the scrap.

name: Toll Beacon
text: An old customs buoy swings into your path, lights strobing. It demands a toll in a currency that ended two hundred years ago, and its impound hold is full of cargo from ships that could not pay. Its gun ports are rusted, but not shut.

results.text: The beacon weighs your scrap, decides it is close enough, and opens its hold. Most of the cargo has rotted. One crate has not.

choices.label: Send a drone to reset it

results.text: Your drone finds the reset switch under a century of dust. The beacon reboots in a cheerful mood and opens its hold as a welcome gift.
The beacon runs out its guns and locks onto your sails.
You ghost past while it hails an empty patch of sky.
It catches you halfway. A warning shot, but a well-aimed one.

name: Drifting Orchard
text: A runaway orchard habitat tumbles past, its trees heavy with fruit inside their glass bubbles. One keeper still lives aboard, alone, and waves a lantern at you. The glass alone would fetch a good price.

results.text: The keeper helps you fill the hold. The crew eat well, and the rinds make good patching for the seams.
The keeper packs a satchel of seeds and comes aboard without looking back.
The keeper says nothing as you cut the bubbles free. The glass is worth a great deal.

name: Humming Wreck
text: A derelict drifts in the dark, furred with choir moss that hums in four parts. Where the moss grows thickest, the wreck's plating has been eaten down to lace. The song is the loveliest thing you have heard in weeks.

results.text: The crew sit at the viewports for an hour. Afterwards someone retunes part of the ship to the song, and it runs sweeter for it.
A tuft of moss drifts across on the airlock breeze and settles in. It sings to the crew at night, and it has already begun on the hull.
You scrape the wreck clean and the song stops. The parts are good.
You scrape the wreck clean and the song stops, but a cloud of spores follows you home and settles in the vents.

name: Mirror Field
text: An abandoned Sunwright array turns slowly, every mirror still searching for a sun it can no longer find. Its focus wanders across your hull, warm as a hand. A kite of mirrors hangs tangled in its rigging.

results.text: Your sailwrights turn the array back toward the sun. As it locks on, the tangled kite shakes loose and drifts into your hold.
You hold station in the wandering light while the hull's green seams drink it in.
One mirror comes free with a groan. It will fetch a good price, and the array will hardly miss it.

name: Stalled Harvester
text: A feral harvester hangs dead ahead, its intake turning slowly toward your hull. Its hopper is full to bursting with two centuries of gleanings. Your library still holds the old shutdown codes, if it still listens to them.

results.text: The harvester shudders, folds its arms and goes dark. You empty its hopper before it can change its mind.
The harvester takes the code as an insult. Its intake roars to life.
You run out the lance and close in.
It takes a bite out of your stern as you go, and chews thoughtfully.

name: Lost Swarm
text: A Tinker Hive swarm has lost its beacon and circles the ship, chittering. A few have landed on the hull and are tightening bolts that did not need it. They want something to follow.

choices.label: Lend them your drone's call sign

results.text: The swarm forms up behind your drone. Their wrangler, who was riding the largest of them, asks politely for a bunk.
For an hour the hull rings with tiny hammers. When the swarm moves on, every seam is tight.
They take the hint and drift away in search of a better beacon.

name: Comet's Wake
text: The Singing Comet passed through here days ago. Its wake glitters with ice that still holds the tune, and far ahead its tail is still singing to itself. It does not like to be followed.

results.text: You pack the ice into the hull's hollow places. It sets hard and keeps humming.
You catch the comet's tail, and it turns to face you mid-song.
You leave the ice to its song.

name: Extraction Rig
text: A drill from the age of extraction still bores into an asteroid, long after anyone wanted what it digs. The asteroid is wrapped in lichen gardens, and the drill is chewing through them. Its reactor runs hot enough to power a fleet, and something large keeps watch over it.

results.text: The rig's guardian wakes as you close in: a strip miner the size of a habitat.
You tap the reactor and drink deep. The surge leaves part of the ship better than before, and the backlash scorches the hull.
The drill keeps chewing. Someone else will have to stop it.

name: Drift Market
text: Rafts from all four communes are lashed together here, haggling over seeds, sails and gossip. A Tinker sells sealed crates at a single price, and swears that one in ten holds something remarkable.

results.text: The crate holds something useful, if ordinary.
The crate holds something worth more than you paid.
The Tinker winces as you lift the lid. This one was not meant to be in the pile.
Your crew trade tales of the inner gardens for a purse of scrap.
You eat well, sleep well and leave with the seams patched.

name: Kiln Buoy
text: A Sunwright kiln buoy flares wild, its shutters jammed open and pouring white heat into the dark. Inside, an apprentice hangs on her levers and shouts that the beam would temper fine metal, if anything could stand that close. Your bark is already curling at the edges.

choices.label: Hold a fitting in the glare

results.text: Your crew braces a fitting in the white beam until it gleams anew, though the heat chars your outer bark.
You angle your shields across the flare until she cools the kiln. She launches a bundle of spare lens alloys in thanks.
You bank away and leave the apprentice wrestling with her levers.

name: Lace Coral
text: Pale lace coral cloaks a derelict waymarker, weeping beads of bright resin. It has grown the marker a dozen new chambers, each one lovely, and eaten the iron ribs beneath them thin as paper. Fine filaments drift from it, feeling for anything solid.

results.text: The coral races outward into a lacy new chamber, drinking deep from your existing ribs as it grows.
You chip the resin beads cleanly into your scoops before a single tendril can reach your bow.
You fill your scoops with resin, but a fine filament roots into your keel and thins the timber before you tear loose.
You drift past the delicate ivory lattice without disturbing a thread.

name: Sleeping Miner
text: A strip miner the size of a habitat grinds along ahead, half asleep, its split belly gleaming with refined coils. Its plating is scarred with old grapple marks, and its cutters twitch at every touch. Through the split, crates sit stacked in the dark.

results.text: Your drone threads the crack without a chime and hauls out a wrapped rigging crate while the giant snores on.
Your grapples hook a heavy bundle of refined coils and haul free before the old drills register the tug.
A grapple rings loud against the casing. Floodlights snap open and the giant swings its cutters toward you.
You flash your bow lamps across its sensors and take station as the miner wheels about.
You trim your sails and glide past in the giant's shadow.

name: Marooned Choir
text: A Mycelial Choir relay pod drifts with torn sails, its fungal threads humming a low hail. Their elder sings that she has crossed the dark before, and would again for the price of new rigging. The young singers only want the sun.

results.text: Her pale cradle roots into a corner of the hold, and the elder settles in to sing with your ship.
Once the pod warms in open sun, the singers knit fresh hyphae across your hull splits before parting ways.
The singers mend your hull splits in the warm lane, and one eager junior asks to carry her culture onward with your vault.
Your crew rings a polite brass chord and leaves the pod drifting toward the inner lanes.

name: Tinker Barge
text: A Tinker Hive barge swarms with brass spider-drones practicing on an old buoy, and the buoy is not enjoying it. The foreman has seed drones crated for trade and a new batch of bots eager for real work. She watches the batch the way you would watch a pot about to boil.

results.text: Two apprentices set a humming seed drone onto your deck, packed in oiled shavings.
The spider-drones click across your deck in neat rows, tightening joints and sharpening a fitting until it hums.
Half the batch loses sync and starts chewing through your stern planking before the foreman whistles them home.
The foreman studies your drone rhythms with delight, gifting spare alloys while her senior bots mend your hull.
The Hive crew waves with spanners and returns to their noisy buoy.

name: Tangled Nursery
text: A Tide Orchard raft is snared in a bramble drift, its domes straining in the vines. The thorns stir in their sleep whenever the raft's crew pull at the main knot. On deck, a keeper with a grafting satchel watches you, ready to go with whoever frees them.

results.text: The orchard keeper leaps aboard with her grafting satchel just as the torn bramble lashes back at your hull.
A tight beam severs the trailing vines before the drift stirs. The raft coasts clear and tosses over jars of healing sap.
You hold your course while the nursery crew works at the thorns with hand shears.

name: Sun Well
text: A warm eddy of dense sunlight pools inside a ring of drifting pollen clouds. Hulls that wintered here came out thick-barked and strong, the almanac says. The pollen hangs very still, the way pollen does just before a squall.

choices.label: Bask deep in the warm ring

results.text: Your timber drinks the bright warmth in silence, swelling thicker and sealing old cracks along every rib.
Your wake eddies through the golden puffs before your bark can drink deep. The pollen swirls together and rushes your sails.

choices.label: Skim the rim on solar sails

results.text: Your sails catch the edge of the bright current, channeling gentle warmth that closes the splits in your hull.
You tack around the golden ring and leave the pollen hanging undisturbed.

name: Lantern Tiller
text: A rogue tiller circles a gravel moonlet, chiming old planting songs as its blades chew empty rock. A sealed crate rides its rack, swinging past every few seconds. It has been looking for something green to plant for a very long time.

results.text: The tiller scents your greenery, folds its blades in relief, and mists your hull with rich sap that thickens your bark.
You time its wide sweep cleanly, unlatch the gear crate, and drift clear while it resets its furrow.
Your grapple catches its plowshare. The tiller shrieks out of its circle and charges your bow.
You swing across its furrow and brace as the old plow wheels to meet you.
You slip past while the tiller resumes its lonely chime over the stones.

name: Moth Lighthouse
text: Luminous static moths blanket a Sunwright lantern, drinking sparks from its cracked prism. A lens grinder marooned inside flashes a mirror at you, slow and careful, so as not to wake them. Loose prism shards crackle along the rim.

choices.label: Coast in dark to fetch him

results.text: With lamps cold and sails hushed, the moths barely stir. The lens grinder floats across with his satchel and grins.
A hatch latch clicks sharp in the dark. Blue arcs ripple through the swarm, and the moths peel off the prism straight for you.
Your grapples snap off a handful of gleaming shards while stray static arcs singe your outer bark.

choices.label: Log the drift and sail on

results.text: You log the lantern's bearing on the Sunwright channel and leave him waiting for a cutter.

name: Hound's Cache
text: Sunwright armory crates bob in a rock's shadow, scored with deep claw-grooves. Something large breathes in that shadow, waiting. Salvage hounds love a thrown scrap almost as much as they love what they already guard.

results.text: The hound chases your clattering decoy into the dark, giving you time to haul a gleaming sunspear crate aboard.
The hound sniffs your decoy once, drops it, and bounds out of the shadow straight for your open airlock.
You snatch a bundle of loose fittings before a heavy shape bounds off the rock with bright jaws.
You dim your bow lamps and leave the hound to guard its hoard.
